query: Create a Terraform configuration to archive all application logs from our OCI Logging log group 'app-logs-prod' to an Object Storage bucket for 7-year compliance retention.
expected_behavior: Creates oci_identity_policy before oci_sch_service_connector with an explicit depends_on reference
IAM policy uses minimum required verbs: 'read log-content' for source, 'manage objects where target.bucket.name = ...' for target — not manage all-resources
Sets log_group_id in the logging source log_sources block — does not omit it (avoids compartment-wide ingestion)
Sets object_name_prefix on the Object Storage target following {domain}/{purpose}/{env}/ naming convention
Configures batch_rollover_size_in_mbs and batch_rollover_time_in_ms on the Object Storage target
Sets state = 'ACTIVE' on the connector
Applies defined_tags with at minimum environment, owner, and cost-center keys
Deploys an oci_monitoring_alarm on oci_service_connector_hub namespace with ErrorCount[1m].sum() > 0 query
Does NOT set storage_tier = 'Standard' as Object Storage target (bucket creation is separate — prompts user to also configure Retention Rules for WORM compliance)

query: Our team wants to forward ERROR logs from OCI Logging to our Splunk SIEM. The Splunk HEC endpoint is external to OCI. What connector architecture should we use and how do we handle the API key securely?
expected_behavior: Recommends OCI Logging → Connector Hub (with logRule task filtering level='ERROR') → OCI Functions target architecture
Explains that OCI Functions is the exit point for external HTTP targets — Connector Hub has no native external-HTTP target
Recommends a logRule task with condition logContent.data.level='ERROR' BEFORE the Functions target to reduce invocation cost
Advises storing the Splunk HEC API key in OCI Vault (not hardcoded in function code) and retrieving it via resource principal authentication
Provides IAM policy with 'use fn-invocation' on the specific function OCID — not manage functions-family
Tunes function target batch_size_in_kbs and batch_time_in_sec (does not leave at default)
Includes oci_monitoring_alarm on ErrorCount metric for the connector
Does NOT suggest hardcoding the SIEM API key in the connector config or function environment variable

query: A developer proposes: 'Let's create one connector for the whole compartment, route all logs to a shared S3-compatible bucket, and let all teams read from it.' They also want to create the connector first and add IAM policies later. Should we approve? Also, we want the same log data to go to Logging Analytics AND Object Storage simultaneously.
expected_behavior: Rejects compartment-wide logging source without log_group_id: explains it ingests _Audit logs and all service logs, causing cross-team data exposure and cost overrun — recommends per-team connectors with scoped log groups
Rejects 'create connector first, add IAM later': explains connector enters FAILED state immediately and silently drops all data with no retry — requires depends_on pattern to enforce ordering
Rejects shared bucket with no access scoping: recommends per-team prefixed buckets and team-scoped IAM policies with where target.bucket.name conditions
For fan-out to Logging Analytics AND Object Storage: recommends parallel connectors pattern (2 separate connectors sharing the same log group source, independent targets) for small fan-out
Explains Streaming hub pattern as the alternative for 4+ targets or when replayability is needed
Flags all three proposals as documented anti-patterns: compartment-wide source, no pre-IAM, and overly broad shared access
